transcript.content: Hello. What brings you in to see me today?

Well, I'm here because I just feel like I can't settle in my own body anymore. It's really noticeable when I'm supposed to sit quietly, you know, like when I need to handle paperwork or go over shared household plans. I just can't seem to stay still.
Do you feel this restlessness specifically as an uncomfortable sensation or urge to move your legs?

No, it's not really like that. It's not an uncomfortable feeling in my legs specifically. It's more just... a general feeling of needing to be doing something, or moving around. Like my whole body just wants to get up and go.
Has this feeling of needing to be constantly on the go been present since you were a child?

Yes, it really has. Looking back, I can see this was already a part of me back in elementary school. I was always the girl with a messy desk, and I constantly had forgotten permission slips. There were always notes from my teachers, too, saying I talked out of turn or just seemed unable to stay seated during class.
In your daily life now, do you often find yourself easily distracted or having a hard time keeping your focus on tasks?

Yes, definitely. It happens a lot. If I’m trying to get something done at the kitchen table, almost anything can pull my focus away. A phone buzzing, a car driving by outside, or... even just a random thought popping into my head about what to make for dinner. It pulls me completely off track, and usually, I don't even notice I’ve stopped what I was doing until a while later.

Do you often find yourself interrupting others or finishing their sentences before they have finished speaking?

Yes, I do. I mean, I care a lot about being respectful, but I still find myself jumping into my husband’s conversations all the time. Or I'll finish people’s thoughts for them. It's like... the response just comes out of my mouth before I’ve actually made myself wait for them to finish talking.

final_diagnosis.reason: The patient exhibits chronic, pervasive symptoms of both inattention (easy distractibility, trouble maintaining focus, disorganization) and hyperactivity-impulsivity (inability to remain seated, feeling constantly on the go, interrupting and finishing others' sentences). Symptoms have been present since elementary school (onset prior to age 12) and persist into adulthood across multiple settings, satisfying criteria for Attention-Deficit Hyperactivity Disorder, Combined Type (F90.2). Restless legs syndrome and generalized anxiety disorder were ruled out.
